mappings.note: A family staying with one local shopkeeper for service and occasional credit rather than the lowest price. How a neighbourhood shop actually works, which is LO-252's subject.
Sorts what travellers really reported about Hampi Bazaar from a false detail. A historical market read from accounts, so the history goal.
India's imports from West Asia. International trade under the economics goal.
What an aggregator does in an online marketplace. Modern market institutions under the goal.
A substandard drug answered by the government's quality-regulation role. The role of government in the economy under the goal.
Sorts the features of a wholesale market from a non-feature. Market types under the goal.
The Arthashastra's rule that ghee sellers add a little extra to offset what clings to the vessel. An ancient text read for trade practice, so the history goal.
Defines demand. Core economic vocabulary under the goal.
Distributor against wholesaler in the supply chain. Market structure under the goal.
India as the largest importer of edible oils. International trade under the goal.

Ima Keithal, the market run entirely by women, and where it is. The goal's clause about recognising the contributions of different sections of society fits this squarely; LO-250 would be wrong, because the market shows women's economic standing rather than a disadvantage.
Defines export. International trade under the goal.
A grain godown against a cold store for perishables. Market infrastructure under the goal.
Market dealings growing into lasting relationships. A general statement about the social side of markets, so the goal; the observed local-shop scenario carries LO-252 instead.
Quality standards for medicines aimed at consumer safety. The role of government in the economy under the goal.
Regulating a chemical factory is the government correcting a harm the market imposes on others (CG-SST4), and the harm itself is river pollution and measures against it (LO-237).
Defines supply. Core economic vocabulary under the goal.
Khari Baoli as a spice market. The geography of specialised markets under the goal; the item asks what is traded, not how the market runs.
Checking weights and measures so buyers get what they pay for. Government protection of consumers under the goal.
Manufacturer against consumer. Market roles under the goal.
Matches market features to their descriptions. Economic concepts under the goal.
Food, water, clothing and shelter classified as basic needs. Economic vocabulary under the goal.
Sorts a wholesaler's real functions from one that is not theirs. The supply chain under the goal.

Sellers adding free haldi and kumkum to a purchase as a mark of auspiciousness - a custom of how local shops actually deal with buyers, which is LO-252's territory rather than an abstract market principle.
A five-star BEE label read as energy efficiency. Standards and consumer information under the goal.
Finds the certification mark wrongly matched to its product category. Standards and consumer protection under the goal.
Accepts the convenience of online markets but rejects the claim that they always cost more. Market types under the goal.
Rejects the claim that online sellers must have physical stores. Market types under the goal.
Fernao Nuniz's list of precious stones sold at Hampi. A traveller's account as evidence, so the history goal.
Rejects the claim that sellers alone fix price and restores the buyer's part in it. The price mechanism under the goal.
Statements on how retailers and wholesalers buy and sell. The supply chain under the goal.
Names the Portuguese traveller who called Hampi the best-provided city. A source-identification item, so the history goal.
Defines a manufacturer. Market roles under the goal.
The BIS mark on appliances and construction materials. Standards and consumer protection under the goal.
Rejects the claim that government has no regulatory role in markets. The role of government in the economy under the goal.
Demand meeting supply to set price. The price mechanism under the goal.
Defines trade in its broad sense. Economic vocabulary under the goal.
Hampi Bazaar's position opposite the Virupaksha temple. Historical topography of a market, so the history goal; the item does not touch temple architecture, so LO-241 would be wrong.
Rising demand for efficient refrigerators read as a signal to producers. The price and demand mechanism under the goal.
A weekly haat set against a multi-storey mall - LO-252 names local markets and shopping complexes together, which is exactly what this item compares.
